name: Heroin
description: Heroin facts: what it is, effects, fentanyl contamination, overdose and naloxone, withdrawal, treatment, and US legal status and penalties.
quick: Heroin is an illegal opioid made from morphine. It is a Schedule I controlled substance in the US, with no accepted medical use. Most of the US heroin supply has been replaced or contaminated by fentanyl, which has made overdose far more likely. Effective treatment with buprenorphine or methadone is widely available.
facts: Dope, smack, H, black tar, junk
Schedule I; no accepted medical use
Prescribed as diamorphine in the UK and for treatment in several European countries and Canada

blocks.p: Heroin is made by chemically modifying morphine from the opium poppy. It crosses into the brain faster than morphine and is then converted back to morphine, which produces an intense rush followed by sedation.[[1]]
It is sold as a white or brown powder or as a sticky dark substance called black tar heroin. Today most drugs sold as heroin in the US contain fentanyl, and many contain no heroin at all.[[2]]

sections.q: What are the effects of heroin, and how long do they last?

blocks.p: Heroin causes a surge of euphoria, flushed skin, dry mouth, and heavy limbs, followed by hours of drowsiness, clouded thinking, slowed heart rate, and slowed breathing ("nodding").[[1]]
Effects begin within seconds when injected and within minutes when smoked or snorted, and last about 3 to 5 hours.

sections.q: What are the risks of heroin?

blocks.p: **Overdose:** heroin slows and can stop breathing. The risk is highest with fentanyl contamination, after a period without use, and with alcohol or benzodiazepines.[[1]]
**Addiction:** heroin is highly addictive. Tolerance builds quickly, and physical dependence develops within weeks of regular use.

**Injection risks:** HIV and hepatitis C from shared needles, skin abscesses, heart valve infections (endocarditis), and collapsed veins. Syringe services programs provide sterile equipment and reduce infections without increasing drug use.
**Xylazine:** a veterinary sedative increasingly found in the heroin and fentanyl supply. It deepens sedation, is not reversed by naloxone, and causes severe wounds.[[3]]

sections.q: What does heroin overdose look like?

blocks.p: Signs of heroin overdose include pinpoint pupils, unresponsiveness, slow, shallow, or stopped breathing, gurgling or snoring, and blue or gray lips and fingertips.[[4]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, cannot be woken, has blue or gray lips, or is breathing slowly or not at all.
Give naloxone (Narcan or a generic nasal spray, sold without a prescription) into one nostril. If there is no response after 2 to 3 minutes, give another dose.
If you are trained, give rescue breaths. Otherwise place the person on their side so they do not choke.
Stay with them. Naloxone can wear off before heroin does, so the overdose can return even after the person wakes up.
Most states have Good Samaritan laws that protect people who call 911 for an overdose from some drug charges.

blocks.p: Never use alone. If you do, tell someone or call a never-use-alone hotline that sends help if you stop responding. Keep naloxone nearby and test drugs with fentanyl test strips.

sections.q: Is heroin addictive, and what is withdrawal like?

blocks.p: Heroin is one of the most addictive drugs. Opioid use disorder is a treatable medical condition, and medicines are the most effective treatment.[[1]]

timeline.title: Early withdrawal
timeline.text: Anxiety, yawning, runny nose, sweating, aching muscles, cravings.

timeline.title: Peak withdrawal
timeline.text: Diarrhea, vomiting, stomach cramps, goosebumps, insomnia, dilated pupils.

timeline.title: Lingering symptoms
timeline.text: Fatigue, low mood, poor sleep, and cravings.

blocks.warn: Tolerance drops within days of stopping. Overdose deaths are especially common after detox, jail, or hospital stays.

blocks.p: Buprenorphine and methadone reduce the risk of death by about half. Extended-release naltrexone (Vivitrol) is another option after detox.

sections.q: Is heroin legal in the US?

blocks.p: Heroin is a Schedule I controlled substance, meaning federal law considers it to have a high potential for abuse and no accepted medical use in the US. It cannot be prescribed.[[5]]

ul: **Possession:** under federal law, a first conviction for possessing any controlled substance without a valid prescription can bring up to one year in prison and a minimum fine of $1,000. Penalties rise with prior convictions.[[6]]

**Trafficking:** trafficking 100 grams or more of a mixture containing heroin carries a mandatory minimum of 5 years in federal prison, and 1 kilogram or more carries 10 years. If death or serious injury results, the minimum is 20 years.[[7]]

**State law:** states set their own penalties, and most drug cases are prosecuted under state law. Penalties range from a civil fine to long prison terms depending on the state, the amount, and prior record.

blocks.p: **Clinical research:** heroin-assisted treatment is used in the UK, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, and Canada (as prescribed diacetylmorphine or hydromorphone) for people who have not responded to other treatment. It is not available in the US.

sections.q: Where can someone get help with heroin use?

blocks.p: Medicines for opioid use disorder work. Buprenorphine can be started by telemedicine and filled at ordinary pharmacies, and methadone is available through opioid treatment programs.[[8]][[9]]

ul: **SAMHSA National Helpline:** 1-800-662-4357. Free, confidential, 24 hours a day, in English and Spanish. It gives referrals to local treatment and support.[[10]]
**FindTreatment.gov:** a federal locator for state-licensed treatment programs, searchable by location, payment, and type of care.[[9]]
**988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline:** call or text 988 for a mental health or substance use crisis.
**Your own clinician:** a primary care doctor can screen, treat, and refer, and can discuss medicines that support recovery where they exist.

blocks.p: Laws change and differ in detail. Check current rules before carrying any controlled medicine across a border.[[11]]

faq: Is heroin the same as fentanyl?
No, but most drugs sold as heroin in the US now contain fentanyl, which is far stronger and causes most overdose deaths.
Yes. Naloxone reverses heroin and fentanyl overdose. It is sold without a prescription.
How long does heroin stay in your system?
Heroin is converted to morphine within minutes. Urine tests detect morphine and the heroin marker 6-MAM for about 1 to 3 days.
Is heroin used in medicine anywhere?
Yes. In the UK it is prescribed as diamorphine for severe pain, and several countries use it in supervised treatment programs.
What is the best treatment for heroin addiction?
Medications for opioid use disorder, buprenorphine or methadone, combined with support. They reduce overdose deaths by about half.
